criteria.check: Detection, banner, queued or flagged writes
criteria.fail_signal: Silent failure offline; data lost
criteria.severity_note: S4 when user-created content is lost; at least S3 for mobile and field apps

criteria.name: Session expiry is graceful
criteria.check: Re-auth in place, work preserved, warnings
criteria.fail_signal: Redirect to login and lose work

criteria.name: Concurrency conflicts handled
criteria.check: Versioning, conflict UI
criteria.fail_signal: Last write silently wins over another user's work

criteria.name: Extreme content safe
criteria.check: Long, zero, huge, null, special characters, missing media
criteria.fail_signal: Broken layout; "undefined"/"NaN"/"null" shown

criteria.name: Large data sets scale
criteria.check: Pagination, virtualization, limits
criteria.fail_signal: Freezes or crashes with large data

criteria.name: Autosave / unsaved-changes guard
criteria.check: Autosave or a navigation guard
criteria.fail_signal: Work lost on navigation
criteria.severity_note: S4 when user-created content is lost

criteria.name: Undo / soft delete
criteria.check: Undo for reversible actions; trash for important objects
criteria.fail_signal: Irreversible delete with no confirmation

criteria.name: Destructive scope clarity
criteria.check: Counts and names in confirmations; type-to-confirm for critical
criteria.fail_signal: "Are you sure?" with no specifics

criteria.name: Permission-denied states
criteria.check: Explain why and how to get access
criteria.fail_signal: Blank, or a raw 403

criteria.name: Not-found states
criteria.check: Helpful 404 for objects and routes
criteria.fail_signal: Crash or blank on a missing object

criteria.name: Rate limit / quota states
criteria.check: Clear limit, reset time, upgrade or wait path
criteria.fail_signal: Raw 429 or generic error

criteria.name: Third-party failure fallbacks
criteria.check: Payment, auth, maps, AI provider failures handled
criteria.fail_signal: Whole page fails when a third party fails

criteria.name: Error monitoring exists
criteria.check: Sentry/Datadog/etc. wired to front-end errors
criteria.fail_signal: Errors invisible to the team

criteria.name: No pre-selected consent or add-ons
criteria.fail_signal: Pre-ticked marketing, sharing or paid add-ons

criteria.name: Symmetric consent choices
criteria.fail_signal: Reject harder than accept; hidden second layer
criteria.severity_note: EU legal risk

criteria.name: No tracking before consent (where required)
criteria.fail_signal: Analytics/ads scripts load before consent

criteria.name: Withdrawable consent
criteria.fail_signal: No persistent way to change consent

criteria.name: No confirmshaming, trick wording, nagging
criteria.fail_signal: Present

criteria.name: No false urgency, scarcity or social proof
criteria.fail_signal: Fabricated timers, stock or activity

criteria.name: Transparent total price
criteria.fail_signal: Fees revealed late; tax or period unclear

criteria.name: Clear trial and renewal terms
criteria.fail_signal: No reminder; unclear charge timing

criteria.name: Cancellation as easy as sign-up
criteria.fail_signal: Phone-only, multi-step or hidden cancellation

criteria.name: Self-serve data export and deletion
criteria.fail_signal: No in-app deletion or export

criteria.name: Privacy notices at collection
criteria.fail_signal: Sensitive data collected without explanation

criteria.name: AI and data-use disclosure
criteria.fail_signal: User data used for training or analysis without disclosure or opt-out

criteria.name: Visibility and sharing clarity
criteria.fail_signal: Users can't tell who sees their content

criteria.name: High-stakes review step
criteria.fail_signal: Money or legal actions without a summary review

criteria.name: Strong, usable authentication
criteria.fail_signal: No password-manager support; no MFA for admin; no passkeys (light)

criteria.name: Safe account recovery
criteria.fail_signal: Insecure or broken recovery; security questions

criteria.name: Session and device visibility
criteria.fail_signal: No session list or security alerts

criteria.name: Sensitive data handled visibly
criteria.fail_signal: Secrets shown unmasked; no re-auth for critical changes

criteria.name: System transparency
criteria.fail_signal: Unexplained denials, failures or automated decisions

criteria.name: Credibility basics
criteria.fail_signal: Missing contact, legal entity, policies or status page
criteria.severity_note: S3 where the law requires the information (legal entity, privacy policy)

criteria.name: Ethical notifications
criteria.fail_signal: No opt-out; manipulative re-engagement

criteria.name: Minors and sensitive categories handled (if applicable)
criteria.fail_signal: No age-appropriate safeguards

criteria.name: Defined type scale
criteria.check: Tokens/variants exist and are used
criteria.fail_signal: No scale; > 8 distinct sizes in use
criteria.severity_note: systemic

criteria.name: Off-scale sizes
criteria.check: Count sizes not in the scale
criteria.fail_signal: Any frequent off-scale size

criteria.name: Body text size
criteria.check: Computed body size
criteria.fail_signal: < 16 px for a general audience; < 12 px anywhere meaningful

criteria.name: Line height
criteria.check: Body and heading line heights
criteria.fail_signal: Body < 1.4 or > 1.8

criteria.name: Line length
criteria.check: Container width for paragraphs
criteria.fail_signal: > ~80–90 characters, or < ~35 for body text

criteria.name: Distinct hierarchy levels
criteria.check: Size and weight steps between levels
criteria.fail_signal: Adjacent levels nearly identical; level order inverted

criteria.name: Weight discipline
criteria.check: Weights in use

criteria.name: Case usage
criteria.check: ALL CAPS and title-case patterns
criteria.fail_signal: Long uppercase text; inconsistent casing across UI

criteria.name: Alignment
criteria.check: `text-align: justify`, centered paragraphs
criteria.fail_signal: Justified or centered multi-line body text

criteria.name: Relative units / scalable text
criteria.check: rem/em/sp/Dynamic Type
criteria.fail_signal: Fixed px everywhere; font scaling disabled

criteria.name: Survives 200% zoom and text spacing
criteria.check: Runtime zoom; fixed-height text containers
criteria.fail_signal: Clipped or overlapping text
criteria.severity_note: WCAG AA

criteria.name: Safe truncation
criteria.check: Ellipsis usage on critical data
criteria.fail_signal: Truncated values with no way to see them in full

criteria.name: Long-string wrapping
criteria.check: overflow-wrap on user content, URLs, emails
criteria.fail_signal: Horizontal overflow or broken layout

criteria.name: Tabular numerals where numbers align or change
criteria.check: `tabular-nums` in tables, counters, prices
criteria.fail_signal: Jittering counters; misaligned numeric columns

criteria.name: Font loading strategy
criteria.check: `font-display`, preload, fallback stack
criteria.fail_signal: Invisible text during load; large layout shift from font swap

criteria.name: Font family count
criteria.check: Families loaded
criteria.fail_signal: > 2 families (excluding monospace) without reason; heavy font payload

criteria.name: Monospace for code and IDs
criteria.check: Code, keys, IDs in monospace
criteria.fail_signal: Code in a proportional font; ambiguous characters (0/O, 1/l/I) in IDs

criteria.name: Readable on all backgrounds
criteria.check: Text over images or gradients has a scrim or overlay
criteria.fail_signal: Text over busy imagery

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.supports: Every WCAG success criterion and threshold cited (contrast 4.5:1 and 3:1, large text 18pt or 14pt bold, non-text contrast, reflow at 320 CSS px, text spacing, target size 24 and 44 CSS px, timing 20 s and 10×, three flashes, focus, redundant entry, accessible authentication, consistent help, dragging).

sources.title: Core Web Vitals thresholds (web-vitals library)
sources.supports: LCP good ≤ 2,500 ms, poor > 4,000 ms; INP 200 / 500 ms; CLS 0.1 / 0.25; TTFB 800 / 1,800 ms.

sources.title: Text size in translation
sources.supports: Translated length relative to English, by source length — up to 10 characters 200–300 %, 11–20 180–200 %, 21–30 160–180 %, 31–50 140–160 %, 51–70 151–170 %, over 70 about 130 %.

sources.title: Recover from validation errors (pattern)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting the pattern page (the page itself was not reachable)
sources.supports: Validate on submit; do not validate when the user moves away from a field; keep answers, add an error summary with focus, show messages next to fields; use novalidate.

sources.title: Error validation (pattern)
sources.publisher: CMS Design System (US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting the pattern page
sources.supports: Validation on submit for most cases; instant validation only where answers are not obvious or fields are hard to complete.

sources.title: Digital Identity Guidelines, Authentication and Lifecycle Management (SP 800-63B-4)
sources.verified_against: Secondary summaries of the final revision (the NIST site was not reachable)
sources.supports: Passwords at least 15 characters when used alone (8 when part of multi-factor authentication); accept at least 64 characters; no composition rules; no periodic forced changes; check against breached and common passwords.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines and design tips (hit targets)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting Apple's design tips page
sources.supports: Controls of at least 44 × 44 pt; the visible control can be smaller than the tappable area.

sources.title: Material Design accessibility (touch targets)
sources.verified_against: Secondary sources citing Material's touch-target guidance
sources.supports: Touch targets of at least 48 × 48 dp, with the visible element allowed inside a larger target.

sources.title: Automated accessibility testing (audit of tools against 142 known issues)
sources.publisher: UK Government Digital Service, cited by the DWP Accessibility Manual
sources.verified_against: DWP Accessibility Manual and GOV.UK guidance (search results)
sources.supports: The best automated tools found about 30–40 % of 142 known issues on a deliberately inaccessible page.

sources.title: Automated testing coverage report
sources.supports: Automated tests covered about 57 % of issues by volume across about 2,000 audits; a vendor figure measured by issue count, not by success criteria.

sources.title: Response Times — The 3 Important Limits (Usability Engineering, ch. 5); after Miller (1968)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting the chapter and Miller (1968)
sources.supports: 0.1 s feels instant; 1 s keeps the flow of thought; 10 s is the limit of attention, beyond which progress feedback is needed.

sources.title: The Economic Value of Rapid Response Time (IBM GE20-0752)
sources.publisher: W. J. Doherty and A. J. Thadani, IBM
sources.verified_against: IBM-hosted copy (figure titles only) and secondary accounts
sources.supports: Productivity rises sharply when system response is under about 400 ms (the "Doherty threshold").

sources.title: The Elements of Typographic Style (3rd ed., pp. 36–37)
sources.supports: 45–75 characters per line for single-column printed text, 66 as a common ideal.

sources.title: A mathematical model of the finding of usability problems (INTERCHI '93)
sources.publisher: J. Nielsen and T. K. Landauer
sources.verified_against: Secondary summaries (CACM 2012 "Sample size in usability studies")
sources.supports: Problems found ≈ N(1 − (1 − λ)^n); with the average λ ≈ 0.31, five users find about 85 % of problems on average. Later studies found 55–100 % for groups of five (Faulkner 2003), so treat five as a per-round minimum for one user group, not a guarantee.

sources.title: System Usability Scale benchmarks
sources.supports: The average SUS score is about 68 (50th percentile); scores are not percentages.

sources.title: First-click studies (Bob Bailey and Cari Wolfson)
sources.verified_against: Searched; no primary or reliable secondary source found
sources.supports: Only the direction is used: a correct first click strongly predicts task success. The often-quoted 87 % versus 46 % is not stated as fact.

sources.title: Inline validation in web forms (A List Apart, 2009)
sources.verified_against: Searched; the 22 % figure appears only in uncited summaries, and later studies report more errors with validation on leaving a field
sources.supports: Not used for any default. Recorded so the old claim is not reintroduced.

sources.title: Label placement in forms (UXmatters, 2006)
sources.verified_against: Searched; secondary sources report findings favouring left alignment for scanning, and the "top-aligned is fastest" claim is disputed
sources.supports: Not used as evidence. Top-aligned labels remain the default for other reasons (narrow screens, translation, design-system practice).

sources.title: Classic HCI laws (Fitts 1954, Hick 1952, Miller 1956, Cowan 2001, Gestalt principles, Iyengar & Lepper 2000, Kurosu & Kashimura 1995, Kivetz et al. 2006)
sources.supports: Qualitative principles only (target size and distance, choice count, memory limits, grouping, choice overload, aesthetic-usability, goal gradient). No numeric threshold in the skill depends on them.

sources.title: Color vision deficiency
sources.publisher: MedlinePlus, US National Library of Medicine
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting MedlinePlus; consistent with Birch (2010, Eye) and a 2025 pooled analysis
sources.supports: Red–green color vision deficiency affects about 1 in 12 males and 1 in 200 females of Northern European ancestry; rates are lower in other populations.
